business_process: Unit operation and power generation (7 units)
description: Control room operation of the seven units using plant process computers, balance-of-plant control systems, and other critical digital assets (CDAs)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reactor safety functions do not depend on business IT; they are protected by design and by the CSP (SYS-05). The values here are planning values for the digital systems that support operation: loss of plant computer functions beyond 8 hours triggers station procedures that may lead to a power reduction. A cyber attack that adversely impacted safety, security, or emergency preparedness functions is a 1-hour NRC notification (10 CFR 73.77(a)(1))
manual_workaround: Control room indications and operator actions under abnormal operating procedures; power reduction or shutdown under station procedures
quantified_impact_basis: Fleet-wide worst case (common-mode event takes all 7 units offline): about $13.2 million of lost revenue plus about $2.6 million of replacement power purchased to meet PPA delivery obligations. One unit offline: about $2.3 million per day
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 CDAs are under the transferred CSP; its site procedures are still the prior owner's (P03 G-020)
single_points_of_failure: None by design (redundant safety trains); common-mode risk on shared digital platforms

business_process: Generator operator dispatch and grid communications
description: Generation Dispatch Center (GDC) real-time communication with host Balancing Authorities and Transmission Operators; unit output and voltage schedules
process_owner: Vice President, Generation Dispatch and Energy Marketing
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: NERC Generator Operator obligations; high impact BES Cyber Systems (CIP-002-5.1a criterion 1.4); real-time data has no useful backlog
manual_workaround: Fail over to the backup GDC at Station 2; recorded voice dispatch from station control rooms
dependent_third_parties: Host Balancing Authorities and Transmission Operators; inter-control-center link carriers
quantified_impact_basis: Plants keep running; cost is scheduling imbalance charges and manual dispatch staffing
single_points_of_failure: Inter-control-center links use one carrier at the backup GDC

description: Protected area access control, alarm stations, intrusion detection, and assessment at the four stations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The security plan requires compensatory measures as soon as a security system is lost; physical security events under 10 CFR 73.1200 have clocks as short as 15 minutes
manual_workaround: Compensatory measures under the security plan (posted officers, manual access control)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Security force (about 900 officers); central and secondary alarm stations
quantified_impact_basis: Per affected station per day: overtime for compensatory postings and slower outage badging
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 security systems are CDAs under its transferred CSP
single_points_of_failure: Alarm station software platform shared by Stations 1 to 3

description: Emergency Response Data System link, offsite notification systems, emergency facility systems, and dose assessment
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: ERDS must be activated no later than 1 hour after declaring an Alert or higher (10 CFR 50.72(a)(4)); a major loss of emergency assessment or offsite communications capability is an 8-hour report (50.72(b)(3)(xiii))
manual_workaround: Backup communications (dedicated lines, satellite phones); manual data transmission under the emergency plan
dependent_third_parties: Telecommunications carriers; state and county emergency management interfaces (DEP-25)
quantified_impact_basis: Direct cost is small; the regulatory and safety impact drives the High rating

business_process: Radiation protection and worker dose control
description: Radiation work permits, electronic dosimetry, access to radiologically controlled areas, dose tracking for station workers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Workers cannot enter radiologically controlled areas without dose controls; dose records must be complete (10 CFR 20.2106)
manual_workaround: Paper radiation work permits; self-reading dosimeters; radiation protection technician coverage at access points
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-13; station radiation protection systems
quantified_impact_basis: Outage case: work in radiologically controlled areas slows by about 30%, delaying critical path work
single_points_of_failure: Electronic dosimetry server at each station

business_process: Work management, clearance and tagging, and surveillance scheduling
description: Work orders, work packages, clearance and tagging (equipment isolation), and Technical Specification surveillance scheduling (about 260 surveillances a week fleet-wide)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Online: a surveillance missed past its Technical Specification interval forces required actions; clearance records protect workers. Integrity matters more than availability (P02)
manual_workaround: Printed daily surveillance schedule and clearance index from the WMS edge servers; paper clearances with independent verification
dependent_third_parties: EAM software vendor (DEP-02); Cloud provider A
dependent_people_or_facilities: Work control centers; operations clearance staff
quantified_impact_basis: Online: deferred work and duplicate paper processing across 7 units
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 uses the prior owner's work management system (DEP-24) until 2027-05
single_points_of_failure: Single fleet WMS instance (edge servers are read-only)

description: Outage schedule, work packages, contractor processing and coordination during a roughly 30-day refueling outage
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Each day of outage extension costs about one unit-day of generation plus contractor standby; WMS RTO tightens to 4 hours during an outage
manual_workaround: Printed work packages and outage schedule; outage control center runs on paper for up to one shift
dependent_third_parties: Major outage contractors A and B (DEP-11, DEP-12)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Outage control center; 1,200 to 1,500 supplemental workers
quantified_impact_basis: About $1.9 million of lost generation per day of extension plus about $1.3 million of contractor standby
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 outages use legacy systems until 2027-05
single_points_of_failure: Two contractors carry about 80% of outage contractor hours

description: Background investigations, unescorted access decisions, badging, fitness-for-duty testing records (10 CFR 73.56; Part 26)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outage contractors cannot start without unescorted access; MTD drops to 12 hours during outages. Personal information must be protected (73.56(m); 26.37)
manual_workaround: Escorted access for urgent work; manual verification calls with other licensees
dependent_third_parties: Shared industry personnel access database (DEP-13); NRC fingerprint processing (DEP-14); background screening vendor (DEP-15)
quantified_impact_basis: Outage case: delayed contractor badging pushes critical path work
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 badging staff use legacy directory accounts

business_process: Engineering, design control, and document management
description: Design changes, drawings, calculations, CDA cyber assessments, controlled documents (EDMS)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Controlled copies of procedures and drawings are held at each station; design changes can wait 2 days
manual_workaround: Controlled hard copies at each station; defer non-urgent design work
quantified_impact_basis: Engineering productivity and deferred design changes
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 drawings partly in the prior owner's system
single_points_of_failure: EDMS in DC-1 with replica in DC-2

description: Fuel cycle contracts, core design data exchange with the fuel vendor, fuel receipt scheduling
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Long-lead activity planned years ahead; fuel deliveries are scheduled months before each outage
manual_workaround: Defer non-urgent transactions; secure email exchange with the fuel vendor
dependent_third_parties: Fuel vendor; enrichment and conversion suppliers
quantified_impact_basis: Minimal daily cost unless an outage is near
single_points_of_failure: Single fuel fabrication vendor per reactor type

business_process: Supply chain, warehousing, and safety-related procurement
description: Purchasing, receipt inspection, warehouse issue of parts, and procurement under the quality assurance program
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Stations hold critical spares; outage parts are staged in advance
manual_workaround: Manual parts issue with later entry; emergency purchase procedure
dependent_third_parties: ERP SaaS vendor (DEP-18); critical parts suppliers
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 warehouse on prior owner's system

business_process: Energy scheduling, PPA settlement, and wholesale sales
description: Day-ahead and real-time schedules with host Balancing Authorities, PPA invoicing and settlement
process_owner: Vice President, Generation Dispatch and Energy Marketing
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Day-ahead scheduling deadlines; PPA invoices about $400 million a month
manual_workaround: Phone and email schedule submission; spreadsheet settlement for one cycle
dependent_third_parties: Energy scheduling and settlement platform SaaS (DEP-21); host Balancing Authorities
quantified_impact_basis: Imbalance charges and delayed settlement cash

description: General ledger, consolidation, SEC filings, SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: MTD drops to 48 hours in the quarter-end filing window (SEC deadlines)
manual_workaround: Manual journal entries; extended close calendar
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and filing risk at quarter end

description: Payroll for 12,000 employees; outage contractor time capture
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Pay dates and wage laws; outage contractor invoices depend on time records
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll; paper timesheets
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 payroll moved to the company in 2025-10

business_process: Monitoring and diagnostics service (fleet and SL-1 clients)
description: M&D center analytics on about 9,600 equipment points for the fleet and 6 external generation owners; advisories and reports
process_owner: Vice President, Monitoring and Diagnostics Services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SL-1 client agreements set report and availability commitments; equipment degradation develops over days
manual_workaround: Station engineers fall back to route-based condition monitoring; clients notified under SL-1 terms
dependent_third_parties: M&D analytics vendor (DEP-16); Cloud provider B
quantified_impact_basis: SL-1 service credits plus lost early warning value for the fleet
acquired_station_dependency: Station 4 sensor gateways report through their own cellular links (P01 R-005)
single_points_of_failure: Analytics vendor without a SOC report

business_process: Dosimetry processing and dose records (fleet and SL-2 clients)
description: Processing about 46,000 dosimeters a quarter; dose reports to the fleet and about 140 external licensees; lifetime dose records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Dose records must be kept until the license is terminated (10 CFR 20.2106(f)); client reporting deadlines in SL-2 agreements; processing must stay with an NVLAP-accredited processor (20.1501(d))
manual_workaround: Hold dosimeters for later reading; issue interim dose estimates from electronic dosimeters
quantified_impact_basis: SL-2 contract penalties and fleet dose record backlog
single_points_of_failure: Dose record database has never been restore-tested (POAM-019)

description: NRC submittals, written follow-up reports, licensee event reports, and inspection support
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Written reports have deadlines of 60 days (10 CFR 50.73(a)(1); 73.77(d)); urgent notifications go by telephone through the ENS, not through IT systems
manual_workaround: Prepare submittals on stand-alone workstations; telephone notifications are unaffected
quantified_impact_basis: Small direct cost; regulatory impact if a written report deadline is missed
